proposals.before: Descending to the Warring States, extravagance and usurpation blazed hotter; they cut away the ritual canopies, probably hating words that harmed themselves.
proposals.after: Descending to the Warring States, extravagance and usurpation blazed hotter; they cut away the ritual registers, probably hating words that harmed themselves.
proposals.reason: Chinese 禮籍 means ritual registers/texts, not canopies; the literal rendering mistranslates 籍.

proposals.before: When Qin swallowed the rival kingdoms it seized their court trains, which is why the Han “great progress” runs eighty-one follow-cars while the statutory halving uses thirty-six.
proposals.after: When Qin swallowed the rival kingdoms it seized their court trains, which is why the great equipage has eighty-one attendant chariots, while the statutory equipage is half that.
proposals.reason: Chinese 故大駕屬車八十一乘，法駕半之 does not name the Han; the idiomatic gloss invents “Han” and restates a count already given as thirty-six.

decisions.reason: Chinese 削滅禮籍 means they destroyed the ritual registers/codices; 籍 is registers or written records, not canopies, and the proposed literal matches that sense.
Chinese 故大駕屬車八十一乘，法駕半之 names neither Han nor thirty-six; the proposal removes those inventions and renders 大駕/法駕半之 as great equipage and statutory equipage half that.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 故大駕屬車八十一乘，法駕半之
